title: Launch: How AI Works
subtitle: Join the AI Creators Guild. Learn what AI really is, how to talk to it, and how to stay safe when you use it.
bigIdea: AI doesn't 'know' things like a person does. It guesses what comes next, using patterns it found in lots and lots of examples. That's why clear prompts matter, and why we always check its work.
objectives: Say in your own words how AI makes words or pictures by guessing from patterns it learned.
Write a prompt with the Guild Prompt Recipe (Role · Task · Details · Style · Format), then make it better step by step.
Spot an AI mistake or an unfair pattern, and check a fact with a trusted source.
Follow the AI Safety Pact: age rules, asking first, privacy, honesty and making your own work.
Explain how XP, levels, houses and Boss Challenges work.

vocabulary.definition: A computer program that learns from examples so it can do jobs like seeing pictures or writing.
vocabulary.analogy: A super fast student who read millions of books but never went outside.
vocabulary.example: Your phone putting all the photos of your dog in one album.

vocabulary.definition: AI that makes new things: words, pictures, videos, music or code.
vocabulary.analogy: A DJ who heard millions of songs and mixes a brand new one.
vocabulary.example: Asking Gemini for a poem about pizza.

vocabulary.definition: The 'brain' an AI builds after learning from lots of examples.
vocabulary.analogy: A recipe book written after tasting a million meals.
vocabulary.example: Gemini is a family of models made by Google.

vocabulary.definition: The examples an AI learns from.
vocabulary.analogy: All the books and practice tests a student studied.
vocabulary.example: Billions of web pages, and pictures with words under them.

vocabulary.definition: What you type to tell the AI what you want.
vocabulary.analogy: Your order at a restaurant. The clearer it is, the better the meal.
vocabulary.example: 'Draw a cartoon cat astronaut, bright colors, square.'

vocabulary.definition: The AI's best guess. AI writes by guessing the next small piece of text, again and again.
vocabulary.analogy: The word guesser on a phone keyboard, but with super powers.

vocabulary.definition: A small chunk of text, like part of a word. AI reads and writes in tokens.
When AI says something false but sounds very sure.
vocabulary.analogy: A friend who makes up an answer instead of saying 'I don't know'.
vocabulary.example: Making up a book that doesn't exist.

vocabulary.definition: An unfair, one-sided pattern. AI copies it when its examples were one-sided.
vocabulary.analogy: If you only ever saw red apples, you'd think all apples are red.
vocabulary.example: Always drawing 'a scientist' as the same kind of person.

vocabulary.definition: Making something better step by step: try it, check it, change it.
vocabulary.analogy: Writing a second and third draft of a story.
vocabulary.example: Prompt try 1 → try 2 → try 3, each one better.

vocabulary.definition: The rules you agree to when you use an app. They often say how old you must be.
vocabulary.analogy: The rules sign at the swimming pool.
vocabulary.example: Many AI apps are only for kids 13 and up.

vocabulary.definition: A fake picture, video or voice that looks real and shows a real person doing something they never did.
vocabulary.analogy: A fake signature, but for faces and voices.
vocabulary.example: A fake video of a famous person selling a scam.

tools.name: Gemini (school account)
tools.bestFor: Main tool for the whole course: chat, explaining things and making pictures, inside the school's Google account
tools.freeTier: Comes with Google Workspace for Education (the school's admin must turn it on)
tools.minAge: Education accounts: all ages. Under-18 accounts get stricter filters and can't edit uploaded photos. Personal accounts: 13+.
tools.classroomUse: The student's main tool. If it's off for students, you run it on your screen and the student tells you what to type.
tools.alternative: You drive Gemini on your screen while the student tells you the prompt

tools.name: Teachable Machine (Google)
tools.bestFor: Training your own tiny picture or sound AI in the browser. It makes 'training data' easy to see.
tools.minAge: No account. Runs in the browser. Point the webcam at things, never at other people without a 'yes'.
tools.classroomUse: Lesson 1: train an AI, then trick it with bad examples.

tools.name: Quick, Draw! (Google)
tools.bestFor: Watching AI guess your doodle as you draw
tools.classroomUse: Warm-up game about how AI finds patterns.

toolsVerified: November 2026 (Gemini for Education age rules checked). Gemini is the main tool for the course.

gamification.questLine: Join the Guild: make your nickname and avatar, learn the rules of AI, and earn your Safety Pact.
gamification.boss: Prompt Duel: hit a target answer in Gemini in as few tries as you can, using the Prompt Recipe. In a group, houses battle. 1-on-1, the student battles the teacher.
sideQuests: Teachable Machine Glitch Hunt: make your AI sure and wrong, and explain why (+25 XP).
Find a real news story about an AI mistake. Tell it in 3 sentences and say where you found it (+25 XP).
Turn the Prompt Recipe into a rap or poem (+25 XP).

safety.teach: Show the tools list. Explain why apps have age rules: laws protect kids' info. No sneaking onto 13+ or 18+ apps. We use school accounts, or the teacher runs the tool.
Webcam and photos of yourself only, and only in class tools. Never other kids. Talk about how a deepfake could hurt someone.
Use Guild nicknames. Never type your full name, school, address, phone number or passwords into AI.
AI guesses what SOUNDS right. Use the Two-Source Rule for every fact.
Using AI is a skill, not cheating, as long as you say you used it. Start using the #MadeWithAI label.

finalProject.title: Prompt Duel + AI Safety Pact
finalProject.brief: Get target answers (like a 4-line poem with special rules, a snack recipe for 6 people with no nuts, or a picture of a certain scene). Use the Prompt Recipe in Gemini. Keep trying until you hit the target, and write down every try. Then write and sign your own AI Safety Pact in your own words. In a group, houses play against each other. 1-on-1, the student plays against the teacher.
deliverables: Prompt Log: try 1, try 2, try 3… with what changed and why
A final answer that matches the target
Your own AI Safety Pact (5 promises in your own words), signed by you (and a parent if you like)

levels: All 5 parts, very clear, plus extra rules or examples
3 or more tries, with a reason for each change
Each change has a clear goal, explained with course words
Checked facts with a source and named the kind of mistake
Promises include 'what I'd do if…' answers

finalProject.levelUp: Write a prompt that turns Gemini into a quiz show host for this module's words. Test it on someone and make it better 2 times.

support: Prompt Recipe card with sentence starters for each part.
Group: pair kids up. One types, one reads the recipe out loud. Swap every 10 minutes. 1-on-1: the student types, you read the recipe.
Word wall with pictures for every new word.
Exit tickets can be answered by drawing and labeling, or out loud.
extension: Run the same prompt in Gemini 3 times. Write down how the answers are different, and why.
Ask Gemini the same thing as 'a pirate' and as 'a scientist'. How does the Role change the answer?
Group: be a Guild Helper during the build. 1-on-1: teach the Prompt Recipe to a family member.

carryForward: The Prompt Recipe, the Safety Pact and the Prompt Log habit come back in every later module.
